- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1316 (in the LAST RUN DIFF); .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1316 in the LAST RUN | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN's new push-from-unresolved-repository branch reads `invocation.warning` (using it as a truthy check) but never emits it. The original PR diff included `_warn(invocation.warning)` immediately before the `unresolved_push_sources.append(...)` call; the LAST RUN stripped that line.
  WHY: When a developer runs `GIT_DIR+=<merged-worktree>/.git git push origin HEAD` from a session checkout on `main`, the guard now asks for confirmation (correctly) but the only `systemMessage` the user sees is "merged-PR guard needs confirmation: could not resolve git push repository; the session checkout may not be the pushed repository." The operator loses the cause-and-effect that the underlying `invocation.warning` carries.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:814-822 (LAST RUN's new test); 833-845 (LAST RUN's other new test) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN's new tests check for substrings inside raw `proc.stdout` instead of structured JSON. They never assert that the underlying `invocation.warning` text reaches the systemMessage.
  WHY: The regression above is not caught by the test suite. A developer reading the LAST RUN's tests gets no signal that an explanatory warning is missing from the user-visible output.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1316 (LAST RUN's new check) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a push invocation has `invocation.warning` set, the new code only adds a generic message to `unresolved_push_sources` and relies on `_request_confirmation` later. It does not also surface the underlying reason (the `invocation.warning` text) anywhere.
  WHY: If the downstream code path (e.g., a future change to `_request_confirmation`'s call site) drops or rephrases `unresolved_push_sources`, the operator will never see what triggered the confirmation.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix: the appended value is no longer applied (if → elif), in both guard copies, which stay byte-identical." (PR DESCRIPTION) and the bug description: "It then still stores <path> in the git environment it checks. Bash appends to the existing variable, so the guard checks a different repository than the one git uses."
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` around line 367 (the second `if name in ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE"):` inside the `+=` handling loop in `_guarded_git_invocations`) and the byte-identical mirror at `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF (the most recent AI autofix run being reviewed) contains no hunk touching that line; the file on disk at `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:367` still has the `if` (not `elif`), so the appended `GIT_DIR+=<path>` / `GIT_WORK_TREE+=<path>` value is still being stored in the `environment` dict that the guard then uses to resolve the push repository. The ORIGINAL PR DIFF in the prompt body DOES include the `if → elif` change in both copies plus the regression test `test_appended_git_override_falls_back_without_using_rhs`, but the LAST RUN's autoscoped editor chose to ship only the confirmation-routing layer on top of code that still has the underlying bug. The two existing test entries the LAST RUN added (`test_unresolvable_worktree_push_asks_when_checkout_is_main` and `test_appended_git_override_asks_when_checkout_is_not_merged`) only cover the confirmation layer, not the `if → elif` fix that closes the security defect the PR description names.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
